papers.title_in_file: Scalable Memory Sharing in Photonic Quantum Memristors for Reservoir Computing
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results text, summary, End Matter D setup; not the full supplementary derivations
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a photonic quantum memristor network with shared memory and simulates it as a quantum reservoir on Fashion-MNIST.

assertions.value: The authors report that, implemented as a quantum reservoir, the memory-sharing network achieves more than a twofold improvement in the combined accuracy-confidence metric over conventional PQMR networks.
quotes: achieving more than a twofold improvement in the combined accuracyconfidence metric compared with conventional PQMR networks
assertions.certainty_reason: One simulated study by the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: The metric is the authors own combination of accuracy and confidence, not accuracy alone.

assertions.value: The authors state that the reservoir has N = 9 memory-shared PQMT units, that the results are simulations, and that the task is three-class Fashion-MNIST with the simplest cyclic ring-type memory sharing.
quotes: The reservoir comprises N = 9 memory-shared PQMT units.
The simulations are performed with the input photon number bound
evaluated for task of three class classification of FashionMNIST dataset
despite employing the simplest form of cyclic ring-type memory sharing
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in End Matter D1 and the Fig. 4 caption.

papers.title_in_file: Designing lattice proteins with variational quantum algorithms
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results overview, HEA results and conclusion text
papers.what_it_is: Tests QAOA variants and a hardware-efficient ansatz for lattice protein sequence optimization in simulation and on IBM Torino.

assertions.value: The authors report that QAOA with a careful choice of mixer yields success probability of at least 0.95 in all instances in noiseless simulations, but its performance drops drastically under noise.
quotes: While the former approach, with a careful choice of mixer, yields good results in noiseless simulations (success probability ≥0.95 in all instances), its performance drops drastically under noise.
assertions.reader_inference: The 0.95 floor holds for the small instances studied (body text ties it to the best mixer and sizes up to N of 16).

assertions.value: The authors report a success probability of at least 0.2 in most instances when running problem-agnostic circuits on a real quantum device with parameters taken from simulations.
quotes: When running the problemagnostic circuits on a real quantum device, with parameters taken from simulations, we obtain a significant success probability (≥0.2) in most instances.
assertions.certainty_reason: One hardware experiment on IBM Torino.

assertions.value: The authors state that problem instances with N > 16 are difficult to solve in the presence of noise, even with a single-layer HEA.
quotes: However, problem instances with N > 16 are difficult to solve in the presence of noise, even with a single-layer HEA.

papers.title_in_file: Case study on quantum convolutional neural network scalability
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, dataset section, discussion and conclusion; skimmed experiment sections
papers.what_it_is: Case study training a simulated quantum CNN on binary classification of small images, compared with a classical CNN.

assertions.value: The author reports that output mean squared error dropped from 0.25 for classical CNN training to 0.23 for QCNN training.
quotes: The hypothesis was partly confirmed in terms of output mean squared error (MSE) - it dropped from 0.25 in the result of classical convolutional neural network (CNN) training to 0.23 in the result of quantum convolutional neural network (QCNN) training.
assertions.reader_inference: A 0.02 gap on a toy binary task is not evidence of a practical advantage.

assertions.value: The author reports a training time of 1.5 minutes for the CNN and 4 hours 37 minutes in the least lengthy QCNN training iteration, and states that the hypothesis was rejected on training time.
quotes: In terms of the training time, however, which was 1.5 minutes for CNN and 4 hours 37 minutes in the least lengthy training iteration, the hypothesis was rejected.

assertions.value: The author states the task is binary image classification, separating a noised image (label 0) from a pure single-colored image (label 1).
quotes: Current outline aims to classify noised image (label 0) and pure single-colored image (label 1).
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 4 states the dataset and labels.

assertions.value: The author states that large training time strongly affects the investigation of quantum neural networks in this case.
quotes: I showed that large training time dramatically influences on investigating quantum neural networks in my case.
assertions.certainty_reason: The author own statement from one study.

papers.title_in_file: Can Variational Quantum Algorithms Demonstrate Quantum Advantages? Time Really Matters
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, Theorem 1 and time-cost discussion, conclusion start (the conclusion text is cut by a page break in the extraction)
papers.what_it_is: Argues that gradient-evaluation cost grows with parameter number in QNNs and estimates ideal VQA running time against classical simulation.

assertions.value: The paper proves that for a general ansatz with L independent parameters and a cost function that is an expectation value under a Hamiltonian, at least O(L) cost-function evaluations are needed to obtain the gradient.
quotes: we need at least O(L) times for evaluating the cost function to obtain the gradient.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1, stated as a proved result in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors report that the ideal time cost easily reaches a 1-year wall time at about 20 qubits.
quotes: The time cost scaling easily reached the 1-year wall time at about 20 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: An estimate under the authors assumptions, not a run.

assertions.value: The authors state that the time-cost analysis is in an ideal setting that does not consider noise, qubit connectivity or reachability, and that the work does not aim to deny the potential of VQAs.
quotes: we do not consider realistic limitations on VQAs like noise, qubit connectivity, reachability, etc.
this work does not aim to deny the potential of VQAs
assertions.certainty_reason: The introduction states the scope of the analysis.

papers.title_in_file: Theory on variational high-dimensional tensor networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, theorem statements, numerical section and discussion; proofs not read
papers.what_it_is: Proves statistical and trainability properties of random high-dimensional tensor-network states, including barren plateaus.

assertions.value: The paper proves that variational high-dimensional tensor-network models suffer from barren plateaus for global loss functions.
quotes: We prove that such variational models suffer from barren plateaus for global loss functions, rendering their training processes inefficient in general.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 5 in the paper, as the abstract states.

assertions.value: The paper proves that for local loss functions the gradient is independent of the system size, but decays exponentially with the distance between the observable and the parameter site.
quotes: for local loss functions, we prove that the gradient is independent of the system size (thus no barren plateau occurs), but decays exponentially with the distance between the region where the local observable acts and the site that hosts the derivative parameter.

assertions.value: The paper proves that the entanglement entropy of random tensor-network states approaches the maximal volume law, except for a small probability bounded by an inverse polynomial of the bond dimension.
quotes: (a) the entanglement entropy approaches the maximal volume law, except for a small probability that is bounded by an inverse polynomial of the bond dimension

assertions.value: The authors state that their numerical results, computed with physical dimension d = 2 and bond dimension D = 2, confirm the analytical results of Theorem 6, and note that the decay may not strictly follow an exponential trend in finite size.
quotes: Here we fix the physical dimension d = 2 and the bond dimension D = 2.
Nonetheless, our numerical results confirm the analytical results presented in Theorem 6.
We note that the decay behavior may not strictly follow an exponential trend.

papers.title_in_file: Efficient hybrid variational quantum algorithm for solving graph coloring problem
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, method overview, discussion of limitations; experiments skimmed
papers.what_it_is: Hybrid hierarchical QAOA and classical greedy algorithm for graph k-coloring, with a subway scheduling application.

assertions.value: The authors state that QAOA determines the coloring within subgraphs while a classical greedy algorithm colors the interaction graph.
quotes: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) is employed to determine the coloring within the subgraphs, while a classical greedy algorithm is utilized to find the coloring of the interaction graph.

assertions.value: The authors state that experimental analysis demonstrates the effectiveness of the algorithm, with rapid convergence of conflict evolution.
quotes: Through experimental analysis, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm, highlighting the rapid convergence of conflict evolution
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors own simulated experiments; no figures read.

assertions.value: The authors state that qubit count constrains the number of vertices and colors, giving the example that with 20 qubits and k = 8, each node needs 3 qubits and at most 6 subgraph nodes can be processed.
quotes: For instance, with 20 qubits and k = 8, the number of qubit encodings that can be represented per node is ⌈log28⌉ = 3, which limits the number of subgraph nodes that can be processed to ⌊20/3⌋ = 6.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own resource limit in the discussion.

papers.title_in_file: Hybrid Parameterized Quantum States for Variational Quantum Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, discussion and conclusion; experiment sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: Introduces HPQS, blending PQC measurements with neural quantum state estimators for shot-efficient variational learning.

assertions.value: The authors report that in expectation-based QML, HPQS yields higher classification accuracy than PQC-only and NQS-only baselines under limited quantum measurements.
quotes: where HPQS yields higher classification accuracy than PQC-only and NQS-only baselines under limited quantum measurements

assertions.value: The authors report that Quantum Parameter Adaptation with HPQS produces LoRA adapter parameters for fine-tuning GPT-2 and Gemma-2 with improved perplexity under low-shot conditions.
quotes: Quantum Parameter Adaptation (QPA), where HPQS produces LoRA adapter parameters for fine-tuning large language models like GPT-2 and Gemma-2 with improved perplexity under low-shot conditions

assertions.value: The authors state that HPQS performance depends on the effectiveness of the classical estimator and the quality of quantum measurements.
quotes: its performance depends on the effectiveness of the classical estimator and the quality of quantum measurements.
